newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - Aug 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - Aug 6.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Sri Lankan political and business stories prepared for Reuters by NewsWatch, Colombo Tel/Fax: 94-1-735182 Internet: lucien@eureka.lk.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy. ------
GOVERNMENT RETIRES DEBT AFTER TELECOM DEAL

The Sri Lankan government is using the $225 million raised from the sale of a 35 percent stake in Telecom to immediately retire 10 billion rupees worth of treasury bills. The decision will save the government 1.5 billion rupees in interest payment this year.
INFANT DEATHS DUE TO INFECTION RISES TO NINE

The number of infants dying as a result of a bacterial infection at the Colombo's Castle Street hospital has risen to nine. Investigations conducted by the Medical Research Institute has revealed that the bacteria, called "Klebsiella" had been brought from outside, possibly through hospital employees or mothers of infant patients. The infection was originally detected on July 23.
POLICE SAYS FIVE LTTE LEADERS INFILTRATE COLOMBO
Police say five leaders of Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) have found their way to Colombo to execute a secret suicide mission.
They said special raids have been launched to arrest the rebels and lodging houses have been warned to be vigilant in letting rooms to people. ------
